terms.gloss: the place where the luggage is collected
terms.comment: A description of ours: no reference work has a word for the baggage reclaim of an airport (searched in Traupman’s travel chapter, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini, and Andresian). It is built on Traupman’s sarcinae and on recipere, the classical verb for getting back what is one’s own. In speech the verb does the work: sarcinās recipere.

phrases.english: Now let’s go and get our bags.

phrases.latin: Exspectēmus dum vidulus noster appāreat. — Ecce, adest!
phrases.english: Let’s wait till our suitcase shows up. — Look, here it is!

sources: Lewis & Short: sarcina · Lewis & Short: recipio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 217.
